I'll calculate this by counting 59 business days starting from 2025-09-17.
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">python3 << 'EOF'
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

# Start date
start_date = datetime(2025, 9, 17)

# Holidays (not business days)
holidays = {
    datetime(2025, 9, 29),
    datetime(2025, 10, 16),
    datetime(2025, 11, 7),
    datetime(2025, 11, 14),
    datetime(2025, 11, 18),
    datetime(2025, 12, 10),
    datetime(2025, 12, 26),
    datetime(2026, 1, 21),
    datetime(2026, 2, 18),
    datetime(2026, 2, 25),
    datetime(2026, 4, 3),
}

# Verify start date
print(f"Start date: {start_date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d (%A)')}")
print(f"Is it a business day? {start_date.weekday() < 5 and start_date not in holidays}")
print()

# Count business days
business_days_count = 0
current_date = start_date

while business_days_count < 59:
    # Check if current date is a business day (weekday and not a holiday)
    if current_date.weekday() < 5 and current_date not in holidays:
        business_days_count += 1
        if business_days_count <= 5 or business_days_count > 55:
            print(f"Business day {business_days_count}: {current_date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d (%A)')}")
        elif business_days_count == 6:
            print("...")
    
    # Move to next day
    current_date += timedelta(days=1)

# Back up one day since we incremented after counting day 59
current_date -= timedelta(days=1)

print()
print(f"Last business day (59th): {current_date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d (%A)')}")
print(f"Answer: {current_date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')}")
EOF
</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

The last business day of the job is **2025-12-16**.
